newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico same-day peso ends lower, wkend dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico same-day peso ends lower, wkend dlr demand.

text.p: Mexico's same-day peso closed 1.9 centavos weaker at 7.6000/7.6030 per dollar on Friday, due to demand from local dealers to cover dollar positions ahead of the weekend, traders said.
"The market is very difficult...first the peso opened firm on the long bond and began to weaken due to dealers who had (dollar) shorts to cover," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and the 24-hour rate meanwhile stood at 7.6210/7.6230 and 7.6160/7.6220 per dollar as the same-day market closed.
The 30-year U.S. Treasury bond yield stood at 6.85 percent, compared to 6.89 in late trade on Thursday, following the publication of U.S. producer price indices.
"Although the market is calmer than recent sessions, dealers are still cautious," another trader said.
"Economic data in both Mexico and the United States have produced no major upsets, but even so I feel that the peso may weaken further before the close," the trader added.
Mexico's trade revised surplus for August was released during early trade. The surplus was revised up to $353 million, compared to a preliminary figure of $264 million.
